explanation: Advance one pointer by one link and another by two. They meet inside a cycle; reaching a null fast pointer proves that the list terminates.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n reachable nodes. Before entering a cycle the pointers take O(n) steps; inside it the relative position closes within one cycle length.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Only two node references are retained.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: If the list terminates, the fast pointer reaches null. If a cycle exists, both pointers eventually enter it and their relative position advances by one cycle position per step, so they must meet. Thus reference equality of the pointers detects a cycle without changing the list.
walkthrough: For values [6,1,9] with setup index 1, the tail node 9 points back to the original node containing 1. Slow and fast pointers eventually meet inside that two-node cycle, so return true. The setup index is supplied to the judge, not to HasCycle. The extra serialized pos is harness setup, not a callable argument; expected is the returned boolean and the harness checks links and values remain unchanged.
edgeCases: Setup index -1 means there is no cycle.
Equal node values alone do not imply a cycle.
The algorithm must not modify links or use a fixed iteration limit.
